title: The structure of human sweetness
authors: Juen Z, Lu Z, Yu R, Chang AN, Wang B, Fitzpatrick AWP, et al.
population: Human TAS1R2-TAS1R3 heterodimer expressed in Expi293F GnTI- cells and purified with a miniGs/gustducin G protein for cryo-electron microscopy; HEK293T cells for calcium-imaging assays of wild-type and mutant receptors
funder: C.S.Z. is an investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute. The early phase of this project was funded in part by a grant from the Berrie Foundation to Rudy Leibel and C.S.Z.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing interests.
result: Cryo-EM structures of the human sweet receptor, a TAS1R2-TAS1R3 heterodimer, bound to sucralose and to aspartame. Both sweeteners bind the same pocket in the Venus flytrap domain of TAS1R2; alanine substitutions of pocket residues (Y103, D142, S165) markedly reduced responses to sucralose in cell-based assays. TAS1R2 binds the ligand and couples to the G protein, and TAS1R3 is an obligatory partner of TAS1R2 for receptor function. The authors state that this single receptor mediates sweet taste in humans and other mammals.
